name: px-toolkit
description: Modding toolkit for Paradox games (Crusader Kings III, Victoria 3, Europa Universalis V): completion, go-to-definition, hover docs, tiger diagnostics, inline localization, event graph and a visual GUI editor.

Reduce VS Code Indexing Load (exclude game assets)
PX: Open Format Docs (.info) for This File
PX: Show Dependencies of Definition at Cursor
GUI Tree: Toggle Ancestors / Subtree Focus
PX: Translate Missing Keys (one by one)
Move Mod (between game folder and project folder)

PX: Exclude This Mod from Indexing

walkthroughs.title: Get started with the Paradox Modding Toolkit
walkthroughs.description: Open your mod, load data from your game patch, and try the current editing tools.

steps.title: Check workspace readiness
steps.description:
Detects your game install, reports whether each dump set is toolkit-provided or generated by you, and offers the game's tiger validator.
[Run Setup & Health Check](command:px.setup)

steps.title: Open your mod folder
steps.description:
Open the folder containing common/, events/ and localization/ as your workspace. The extension indexes it and watches for changes.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

steps.title: Generate both game-data dumps (recommended)
steps.description:
For your installed patch, generate script_docs and the data-type dump. They cover different parts of completion and hover. See the steps for your game.
[Reload both dump sets](command:px.reloadScriptDocs)

steps.title: Enable tiger diagnostics
steps.description:
The game's validator checks your mod and shows problems in the editor. Download it, then use Validate Mod in Project or the validator in the status bar.
[Download validator](command:px.downloadTiger)

steps.title: Try it
steps.description:
Open an event file, hover an effect, then right-click an event or localization key and choose an action from the Paradox menu. Press Shift+F10 for the same menu from the keyboard.
[Insert Snippet](command:px.insertSnippet)
[Export Generated Snippets](command:px.exportSnippets)

steps.title: Explore the Paradox view
steps.description:
The Paradox icon in the Activity Bar opens the Project view and the mod overview: content inventory, problems, localization coverage, overrides and the event graph.
[Show Event Graph](command:px.showEventGraph)
[Show Mod Report](command:px.modReport)

px.gamePath.markdownDescription:
Path to the active game's data folder, e.g. `.../steamapps/common/Crusader Kings III/game`. Powers completion, hover and go-to-definition on vanilla content. Which game is active follows `px.gameId`.

**Easiest:** leave empty and run `Paradox: Run Setup & Health Check` — it finds the game via Steam and fills this in. Opening the game folder as an extra workspace folder also works.

px.logsPath.markdownDescription:
Folder containing the `script_docs` dump files (`triggers.log`, `effects.log`, `event_targets.log`, `modifiers.log`). Leave empty to auto-detect it per game: `Documents/Paradox Interactive/<game>/logs` for CK3, `<game>/docs` for Victoria 3 and EU5.

The dumps match the engine vocabulary to your exact game version (bundled snapshots are used until you dump your own): launch the game with `-debug_mode`, run both `script_docs` and `DumpDataTypes` (CK3) or `dump_data_types` (Victoria 3/EU5) in the console, then run `Paradox: Reload Game Data`.

px.tigerPath.markdownDescription: Path to your own tiger binary (`ck3-tiger` or `vic3-tiger`, matching the active game). Leave empty to use the copy installed by `Paradox Tiger: Download or Update Binary` (also offered during Setup).

enumDescriptions: Detect from the mod's descriptor shape: descriptor.mod → CK3; .metadata/ plus in_game|main_menu|loading_screen stage folders → EU5; .metadata/ alone → Victoria 3; otherwise CK3.
Europa Universalis V (community-sourced schema; not yet verified against a live install)
px.gameId.markdownDescription: Which game this workspace mods. `auto` detects from the mod's descriptor shape and is right for almost everyone; set explicitly when detection guesses wrong. `px.gamePath`/`px.logsPath`/`px.tigerPath` always describe the ACTIVE game and are honored when set; unset paths are auto-detected per game (Steam library / Documents). Games without a tiger build (EU5) skip tiger integration.

px.notifications.startup.markdownDescription: Show optional setup notices when a mod workspace opens. Configuration errors still appear. Notice details are recorded in the Paradox Modding Toolkit output.

px.modPath.markdownDescription: **Leave this empty** unless your mod folder is not part of the workspace. Every workspace folder that is a mod of the active game is detected and fully indexed automatically. Features follow the file you are editing, and the sidebar views follow it too (or a mod you pin via `Paradox: Pick Focus Mod`).

px.modProjectsDir.markdownDescription:
Optional folder for mod PROJECTS, the layout that keeps git history, notes and the Steam Workshop listing files outside the mod folder: each mod gets its own subfolder there with the real mod content in `<project>/mod` and the listing in `<project>/workshop`. The game finds the mod through a link in its own mod folder (a `<name>.mod` path file, or a folder link for the metadata games).

The default layout needs no setting: the mod lives in the game's mod folder and a `.pxignore` file keeps git, editor and toolkit files out of toolkit uploads. `Paradox: New Mod` offers both.

px.parentMods.markdownDescription:
Dependency mods your mod builds on, for submods and compatibility patches. Absolute paths in load order, base first.

Parents are read-only context: their definitions resolve in completion, hover and navigation, but they are not validated or edited. Do **not** list mods you are editing — open those as workspace folders instead (*File → Add Folder to Workspace*) and they are picked up automatically.

Shareable per-mod alternative: `<mod>/.px-toolkit/playset.json` with `{ "parents": ["path/to/parent"] }`.

px.excludedMods.markdownDescription:
Workspace mod folders to skip entirely (absolute paths). Excluded mods are not indexed: no completion, hover, navigation, diagnostics or views. Useful when the workspace contains mods you are not currently working on.

Easiest via the per-mod switches in the sidebar Project view, or `Paradox: Exclude Workspace Mods from Indexing`, which shows a checklist of the detected mods.

px.locLanguage.markdownDescription: Localization language to index and display (matches `l_<language>` yml files), e.g. `english`, `french`, `german`.

enumDescriptions: Run on every save of a mod script file (debounced).
Run only via the 'Paradox Tiger: Run Validation' command.
px.tigerRunOn.markdownDescription: When the tiger validator runs (`ck3-tiger` / `vic3-tiger`, whichever matches the active game).

px.diagnostics.ignore.markdownDescription:
Diagnostic codes to suppress everywhere. Applies to the extension's own structural/localization codes (e.g. `missing-bom`, `unknown-event`) and to tiger report keys (e.g. `unknown-field`).

For single lines, an inline `# px:ignore <code>` comment does the same.

px.diagnostics.ignorePatterns.markdownDescription: Glob patterns matched against workspace-relative file paths; all diagnostics (ours and tiger's) in matching files are suppressed. Supports `*` (within a path segment) and `**` (across segments), e.g. `common/**/vendor/*.txt` or `*.generated.txt`.

px.diagnostics.vanilla.markdownDescription: Diagnose files under `px.gamePath` (vanilla game content). Off by default: the extension only ever diagnoses your mod's files.

px.diagnostics.requireDescriptor.markdownDescription: Report an error (and offer to create one) when a mod folder has no `descriptor.mod` / `.metadata/metadata.json`. Off by default.

enumDescriptions: Insert documented fields with blank values and Tab stops. Fields marked optional are omitted.
Insert documented example blocks and scripted-call parameters.
px.completion.mode.markdownDescription: What accepting a script keyword completion inserts. Minimal keeps the fields from valid documented examples and leaves their values blank; unknown syntax stays a name. Explicit definition templates and **Paradox: Insert Snippet** still insert their full templates. Changes apply immediately.

enumDescriptions: Head, facts and provenance only. No prose, no example, one meaning.
Everything, with caps: 3 meanings, 3 example lines, 2 doc paragraphs.
Example cap lifted, every distinct meaning, scope chain always shown.
px.hover.detail.markdownDescription: How much a hover shows. Longer examples and extra meanings stay reachable from the disclosure inside the hover, so `standard` hides nothing permanently.

px.texturePreview.background.patternErrorMessage: Use checkerboard, dark, light, or a six-digit hex color such as #808080.
px.texturePreview.background.markdownDescription: Background for DDS editors and texture hover previews: `checkerboard`, `dark`, `light`, or a hex color such as `#808080`. The DDS editor's palette changes this choice for the workspace. Files and exported PNGs keep their transparency.

px.scopeInlayHints.markdownDescription: Show the inferred scope (e.g. `character`) after scope-changing block openers like `every_vassal = {`. Best-effort inference; display only.

px.indexAssets.markdownDescription: Index definitions and references in graphics `.asset` files for supported games, across mods, dependencies and vanilla. Disable to reduce indexing time and memory. Changing this rebuilds the index automatically. Syntax highlighting, folding and on-demand texture previews remain available.

px.calendar.markdownDescription: Fallback for mods without their own calendar file. A mod declares its display calendar in `<mod>/.px-toolkit/calendar.json` (`Paradox: Declare Calendar` writes it): one per mod, committed with it, read wherever the mod is opened, and it wins over this setting. Same shape here: `{ "epoch": 4000, "after": "AD", "before": "BC" }` makes script year 3000 display as `1000 BC` and 4000 as `1 AD` (inlay hints + hover, `Paradox: Insert Date`). Optional `months` replaces the standard 12: `[{ "name": "Narvinye", "days": 30 }, ...]`. Window-scoped, so it can hold one calendar per window and a `.vscode/settings.json` inside a mod subfolder is ignored by VS Code. `Paradox: Generate Calendar Localization` writes the matching game-side loc (era math + date-format overrides) into the mod.

epoch.description: Script year displayed as year 1 of the later era.

after.description: Era label for script years at or after the epoch (e.g. AD).

before.description: Era label for script years before the epoch (e.g. BC). Omit for a single-era calendar. Must differ from the later era's label.

months.description: Custom month names and day counts, first month first. Omit for the standard 12 months. The names must be distinct.

px.enableForWorkspace.markdownDescription: Escape hatch: set to false to stop this workspace's txt/yml files from being switched to the Paradox language modes.

px.sidebar.hidden.markdownDescription:
Command ids to hide from the Tools section of the sidebar Project panel, e.g. `px.imageGuidelines`. A group whose rows are all hidden disappears with them.

Easiest via `Paradox: Customize Project Panel Rows`, which shows a checklist of every row.

px.workshop.dir.markdownDescription:
Where a mod's Steam Workshop listing lives as files, resolved against the mod's content folder (absolute paths work too). Empty: `.px-toolkit/workshop` inside the mod, which a toolkit upload leaves out (see `.pxignore`), or an existing `workshop` folder next to the mod (the `<project>/mod` + `<project>/workshop` layout).

The folder is the store the Workshop panel reads and writes: `description.bbcode`, `translations/<language>/title.txt` + `translations/<language>/description.bbcode` per translation, `item.json`, `previews/`, `dependencies.json`, `changelog/`. A `description.md` left from an earlier version is converted to BBCode once, the first time the panel reads the folder.

px.workshop.changelog.markdownDescription:
Where the Workshop panel looks for changenotes, resolved against the workshop folder (`px.workshop.dir`; absolute paths work too).

- **A folder** (the default `changelog`): the file named after the descriptor's version is used - `1.2.md`, `v1.2.bbcode`, `1.2.txt`.
- **A single file with headlines**: the section under the headline containing the version is used (`## 1.2.0` in Markdown, `[h2]1.2.0[/h2]` in BBCode).
- **A single file without headlines**: the whole file.

Markdown is converted to Steam BBCode on the way.

The Workshop panel's changenote dropdown offers any changelog the mod already keeps (a `CHANGELOG.md` at the mod root, for instance) and writes this setting for you.

px.coaLibraryDir.markdownDescription:
Folder where the Coat of Arms Designer stores coats of arms as script files. Empty: `Documents/Paradox Interactive/<game folder>/px-toolkit/coat_of_arms`.

The library is outside any mod, so a design survives the mod it was drawn for. Each file holds one `NAME = { … }` definition, the same text the designer's Copy button puts on the clipboard, so a stored design can also be pasted into a mod by hand. The folder is created on the first export.

px.trace.server.markdownDescription: Trace the communication between VS Code and the language server (for debugging / bug reports).

px.trace.perf.markdownDescription: Log how long the language server spends on each request, file rescan, index change and indexing phase to the *Paradox Modding Toolkit* output channel. Off by default; turn it on when reporting a slow save or slow completion, then paste the `perf …` lines into the report.

px.dev.webviewSource.markdownDescription: **Toolkit development only.** Absolute path to a toolkit checkout's `packages/vscode/dist/webview` folder. When set, panels load their app bundles from there instead of the installed extension and reload themselves when a bundle is rebuilt (`pnpm run watch:webviews` in the checkout). Leave empty unless you are working on the toolkit itself.

args.markdownDescription: Options passed to the game. Common ones: `-debug_mode` (debug tooltips + console), `-develop` (hot reload of saved files), `-mapeditor` (open the map editor), `-continuelastsave` (load the last save), `-skip` (CK3: straight to the 1066 lobby), `-play=e_hre` (CK3: skip the menu and play the holder of a title), `-random_seed=42` (fixed RNG seed, needs `-debug_mode`), `-benchmark` (automated performance run), `-nographics` (headless observer game). Empty array = vanilla launch.
